blocks.text: Barkpark Tasks · mobile epic preparation · lane: product-shapes · 2026-07-23

content.value: Barkpark Tasks: three rival shapes — the Minimal, the Maximal, and the Sweet Spot

A mobile app that is not Barkpark itself but rides its core: Cloud login, then server → workspace → project → dataset with one-option auto-select and last-location memory, then three surfaces — tasks, chat, papers. This paper develops the three product shapes the wish demanded to real-sketch depth, names the endpoint behind every screen, and recommends the Sweet Spot — the Operator's Leash — as a staged path THROUGH the Minimal, built on one bet the platform has already proven twice: all three surfaces are PortableDoc surfaces, and the app is the fourth sibling client of live machinery. The crown paper for the stack is barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone.

items.label: median paper payload with fields= metadata projection (vs 137 KB full) — measured live on guerrilla
chat block types already render identically on Studio, TUI and @barkpark/react — zero renderer-parity risk for mobile chat
hits for APNs/FCM across api/ and cloud/ — native push is the one place 'just a new client' becomes new backend
the smallest token that reads tasks + papers + search AND drives chat (write is only needed to create documents)

content.value: What we will create — the verdict

Recommendation: build the Sweet Spot — the Operator's Leash — as a staged path whose v1 IS the Minimal shape plus three welds (chat⇄tasks hand-task strip, universal search, needs-you push). The architectural bet: task briefs are PortableDoc envelopes (docs/setup/TASK-SYSTEM.md:45 on origin/main), chat messages persist server-rendered blocks alongside source_markdown (chat charter D8), and papers ARE PortableDoc. The Go TUI is the existence proof that a thin client composing one renderer with the task API and the chat API can be excellent at all three surfaces. The mobile app is structurally the third instance of that proven composition — 'One Chat Two Surfaces' explicitly anticipated siblings, and the Studio board's own evolution already reached the phone: wave 18's deck replaced kanban with a rail of literal 9:19.5 phone-frame cards, live on main today.

Ship v1 as a Reader-Communicator with teeth: read-only task browsing on the TUI's spine + criteria-first grammar, the full chat floor (send / stream / interrupt / approve-deny with draft continuity), a premium cached paper reader, one search box — plus needs-you push notifications, promoted INTO v1. Three lanes independently converged on the lock-screen approval as THE reason a mobile app should exist; deferring it to v1.5 would ship an app without its killer moment. This is the single deliberate 'new backend' exception, and the server signal to hang it on already exists: the herd layer's Dispatcher-native chat_blocked source and BlockedSweeper (chat charter D57h/D58h). The crown paper must ratify this ruling — it is the largest scope judgment this lane makes.

blocks.caption: The shared skeleton every shape inherits. Auto-select (1 option = skip) and last-location memory are CLIENT-side below the Cloud layer: workspace/project/dataset rows are bare {id, slug, name} with no counts or last-used hints; only the project level carries a server-side 'default'-first ordering (tenancy.ex:858-869). The device-login + fleet-pick cascade is NOT new design — it shipped for the CLI wizard (.claude/workflows/bp-login-ux-charter.md, waves 1-3 merged) and mobile becomes its fourth consumer.

content.value: The mobile app is not a new product surface. It is the fourth client of machinery that already ships — one renderer, two protocols, and a login flow that already exists.
Shape A — the Minimal: 'Reader-Communicator'

The least app that is still excellent. Three tabs and a search box; zero mutations outside chat. Its honest floor is higher than 'read-only' sounds: an agent chat without approve/deny is broken, so the needs-you triple (approval / question / plan — unified server-side, all riding POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/approval with {request_id, decision: allow|deny}) is IN the minimal shape. Task reading ports the TUI grammar that already survived contact with users: one ordered spine (epics → clusters → loose), '+N more' fold rows as tappable affordances, enter-descends/esc-ascends mapped 1:1 to push navigation, criteria-first detail where every section is conditional and color means state only.

content.value: No task verbs, no task creation, no paper editing, no notifications, no host/provider controls, no multi-server switching, no media browsing. Deliberate absences are the shape's identity: every one of them is reachable by a deep link into Studio (the TUI already ships o → Studio task URL as an SSH-friendly escape hatch; the app inherits the same move).

blocks.title: What the Minimal deliberately does NOT have

content.value: Shape B — the Maximal: 'Pocket Studio'

Everything the platform offers. The task tab becomes the full board — deck of phone-frame cards (already designed and live at /admin/projects, board_live.ex wave 18), gantt expand (wave 21), peek family-tree inspector (waves 13-15), drag restage through the same fenced claim/close/release primitives agents use (restage_plan/4, board.ex:645-662). Chat reaches full ChatLive parity: ~40 handle_events including provider/model/effort pickers, execution-target and registered-host selection, bypass arming ceremony, fleet rollup herd view, slash commands, context ring. Papers gain block editing. Plus media, multi-server fast-switch, and lock-screen push approvals.

For: Studio LiveView already proves every interaction server-side — a maximal client is transcription, not invention; the ChatLive render-vocab census gives a complete parts list. Against, and decisive for this lane: three of its pillars are NOT 'just a client'. (1) Native push has zero existing machinery — grep across api/lib and cloud/lib finds no APNs/FCM; the filed scc-w13-notify-channels task is Web Push + webhook only. (2) Paper block editing exceeds EVERY non-admin token today: all three ops routes sit behind RequireIngestToken (shared ingest secret OR admin api_token — require_ingest_token.ex has no write/chat path). (3) Nine ChatLive surfaces are LiveView-only and never reach any client today (MCP entity chips, thinking pulse, compaction notice, context ring, slash menu, provider/host pickers, bypass ceremony, Doing strip, session chrome) — each must be reproduced, proxied, or scoped out. The Maximal is a fine v3 horizon, not a v1.
Shape C — the Sweet Spot: 'Operator's Leash'

A genuine synthesis, not a midpoint: the Minimal's reading excellence plus the one thing a phone is FOR — being reachable when your agents need you. Three welds define it. Weld 1, chat⇄tasks: Studio already prototyped the hand-task picker (Tasks.ready limit 8, chat_live.ex:544) and the Doing strip above the composer (:281-282, :555) — the app ports both, making 'hand this ready task to the running session' a first-class phone gesture. Weld 2, universal search: FTS already spans tasks + papers with facets and a fields= projection at ~1 KB per hit. Weld 3, needs-you push: one notification channel keyed on the pending-ask rows the BlockedSweeper already watches (D58h keys on ask rows, never agent_state), deep-linking straight into the transcript's approval card. The herd home (blocked > stalled > working > idle, deterministic sort, 150s stall badge — herd.go:245-287) is the natural launch screen for an operator with more than one session.

The open home-surface question — three equal tabs vs a cross-surface needs-you inbox (approvals + blocked tasks + lease-expired in one feed) vs chat-as-home — is left deliberately open. No existing surface has designed a cross-surface inbox, so it has no prior art to port; the safe v1 answer is three tabs with a needs-you badge count, letting the inbox graduate to home in v1.5 if usage proves it.
What we learned — findings, surprises, corrected premises

Fourteen storm probes fed this lane. The central discovery held: the three surfaces are one rendering problem plus two protocols. But several of this lane's founding beliefs were corrected by evidence, and the corrections change the product brief:

The editing machinery exists (pd-everything-editable, 19 children, graded A-); the wall is RequireIngestToken (ingest secret OR admin only). The cheap seam: Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — a surgical plug change

content.value: Findings that make the app cheaper than it looks

items.value: One renderer covers everything that matters: @barkpark/react dispatches 66 block types (CI-pinned), including all 6 chat blocks; the only missing types are the 15-item schema/field family (field-*, arrayOf, composite, codelist, localizedText, embed) — structured-data blocks, not prose or chat. Chat has zero renderer-parity risk on any shell choice.

The interaction grammar transfers wholesale: spine ordering, fold rows, criteria-first conditional detail, color-as-state-only, the deck's 9:19.5 phone cards, the double-press close guard, the 8s interrupt wedge, the 150s herd stall badge — all shipped, all numbered decisions with file anchors.

The pull keyset events feed (GET /v1/tasks/events?since → {events, cursor, has_more}) is background-kill-safe — cache the cursor, replay on foreground — strictly better for phones than SSE, which iOS suspends. The platform accidentally built the ideal mobile sync primitive.
Cross-device draft continuity already exists: D14 PATCHes draft/mode/model/effort on leave and re-GETs on resume — a draft typed on the phone resumes in the desktop TUI with no new server work.
Paper payload economics are settled: 1.4 KB metadata / 34 KB blocks / 137 KB full (median, measured live) — prefetch dozens of papers for offline browse, fetch blocks on open.
Reader excellence is cheap: 5 block types cover 92% of all authored block instances; nail ~6 families beautifully, degrade the tail honestly (all 18 formerly-unstyled families now have CSS on main).

content.value: Findings that constrain the design

items.value: Tenancy depth differs per tab — the wish's 5-level cascade lands at a DIFFERENT level per surface: chat is workspace-scoped (RequireChatAccess), tasks are flat host-root (any token), papers/data are dataset-scoped. The app's scope object must carry all levels; each tab consumes the level it needs. One cascade UI, three effective scopes — a crown-level fact, not a bug.

Media in a WebView: paper image src values are bare unsigned /media/files/ strings; serving is public by DEFAULT visibility but token/private assets silently 403 (a WebView cannot attach Bearer headers, and nothing pre-signs at render time). Honest v1 promise: excellent reading for public-visibility media; scoped/private needs a signed-src or fetch-to-blob shim later. studio_chat.ex:2441 already flags this exact leak class.

Chat requires a live managed runtime or enrolled chat host — a phone cannot run the CLI. Live probe: all 37 guerrilla sessions are provider=claude, execution_target=managed; on a vanilla self-hosted box the chat tab may be dead-on-arrival and needs the empty-state/onboarding screen no sibling surface has designed (lane-3 territory; the brief cannot dodge it).

The chat-transcript rendering fork is real and couples to the shell bet: this lane's evidence favors persisted blocks through the shared renderer (D8 ships blocks server-side; 6/6 JS parity); the shell lane argues native rendering from source_markdown. One ruling, in the crown, after the shell verdict.

iOS reality checks (if the shell is a PWA): installed PWAs get NO storage-eviction exemption (heuristic safety via persist() + regular opens), Web Push is install-only, SSE never survives backgrounding — reconnect-on-foreground is law regardless of shell. The 'instant open + remember where I was' promise is only CONDITIONALLY honorable as a PWA; native/Expo carries none of these caveats (expo/fetch streams since SDK 52; App Store risk is low — guideline 4.8 explicitly exempts first-party-account apps; keep all billing web-side).

content.value: How the system works today — anchors a builder can jump to
The chat wire contract (the app's most intricate dependency)

blocks.value:
POST /v1/chat/sessions                {mode?,model?,effort?} -> 201 session (id = CLI --resume key)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions?archived=      -> {sessions:[...]} sidebar shape (+agent_state, D50h)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions/:id[?since=n]  -> full session + messages seq-asc; assistant rows carry
                                         blocks (server FromMarkdown, D8) AND source_markdown
PATCH /v1/chat/sessions/:id           {draft|mode|model_choice|effort_choice|title} strict allowlist
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/messages   {content} -> 202 {accepted:true}   (queued badge = client-only, D12)
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/interrupt  -> 202 {request_id} (ack is semantically EMPTY; truth = result frame)
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/approval   {request_id, decision:allow|deny} -> 204  (D22: nothing richer)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions/:id/events     SSE: replay (id:<seq> event:message) then live (event:chat,
                                         verbatim provider frames, no id); event:permission; event:exit;
                                         keepalive 30s. Turn settles ONLY at the terminal result frame (D8).
GET  /v1/chat/events                  fleet stream: snapshot(50-cap)/state/heartbeat frames,
                                         Last-Event-ID = opaque epoch:seq (D45h)
Auth: [:api, :require_chat_access] — global admin OR workspace-bound 'chat' token (Connectors D18).
Bounds: title/request_id <=256B; content/draft <=64KiB. Transcript window: 500 rows.
Sessions spawn lazily on first send, never on mount; reopen replays history instantly.

content.value: The client discipline is fully codified in the chat TUI's numbered decisions — the mobile parity checklist is: D5 (caller owns the SSE cursor, seeded from max persisted seq), D8 (settle at result frame; then ONE tail refetch with ?since), D9 (live deltas are truth until settle, then discarded), D11 (interrupt mid-turn; 8s client wedge timer force-degrades), D12 (queued badge is pure client state), D14 (PATCH continuity set on leave, re-GET on resume), D51h (idle back-gesture detaches, never interrupts), D53h (stall computed fresh at render, never stored). Reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary replaces any assumption of a durable stream.

content.value: Task reading, sync, and the pagination law

items.value: GET /v1/tasks: limit clamped [1,1000], offset [0,100000]; default order desc(updated_at), desc(id) — UNSTABLE for paging a live ledger (3400+ tasks under constant multi-agent mutation). Stable orders already exist: parent= filtered views use asc(inserted_at), asc(id); /v1/tasks/ready uses priority asc, inserted_at asc, id asc. Mobile law: never bulk-sync the default order; page a stable order, or prime + events.
GET /v1/tasks/events?since=<id> → {ok, events, cursor, has_more}, monotonic cursor, ≤500/page — the mobile sync spine: persist the cursor, replay on foreground.

Task brief is a presentation-grade PortableDoc envelope; detail rendering = the same problem as papers (one renderer). Criteria-first reader order is shipped TUI law (detail_render.go D15) even though its doc codification is still an uncommitted local edit.

The board's deck (default view, wave 18) proves the phone card: 9:19.5 phone-frame cards, click expands to family gantt (wave 21); the kanban drag surface does NOT transfer to portrait — the spine/deck/peek lineage does. BoardLive has exactly 9 handle_events; restage fans into claim/close/release/refuse via pure restage_plan/4.

content.value: Risks and unknowns

(1) Push in v1 makes the first release depend on the one genuinely new backend build — if it slips, v1 ships as the Minimal and push becomes v1.1; that graceful degradation is exactly why the shapes are staged. (2) Chat-tab dead-on-arrival on servers without a managed runtime — needs the onboarding empty state; severity depends on lane 3's runtime findings. (3) The eventual-editing ambition contradicts the v1 token design ([read,chat] cannot edit papers); resolved only by scheduling the auth seam in v2, and the crown must carry that dependency visibly. (4) Offset paging on the live ledger will corrupt task lists if a builder ignores the stable-order rule — the epic brief must state it as law. (5) If the shell is a PWA, the cache promise is conditional on iOS heuristics and Web Push is install-only; the shell lane's verdict may force native for push alone.

(1) RATIFY push-in-v1 (this lane recommends yes; it breaks 'new client only' purity). (2) The v1 task-verb line: pure read (recommended) vs shipping claim/close in v1. (3) Home surface: three tabs with badges (recommended for v1) vs needs-you inbox as home vs chat-as-home. (4) Whether the dataset level appears as a real cascade screen or lives only inside a scope switcher (auto-select hides it 99% of the time either way). (5) The chat-transcript rendering fork — persisted blocks through the shared renderer vs native from source_markdown — rule it once, in the crown, after the shell verdict. (6) Paper-editing staging: prose-only v2 (recommended) vs 'continue in Studio' handoff forever.

content.value: This paper is the product-shapes lane of the Barkpark Tasks mobile preparation stack. The crown paper — barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone — combines it with the identity-cascade, chat-third-client, tasks-papers-reading, and shell-and-cache lanes, and must rule on the four forks this lane leaves open: push-in-v1, the v1 mutation line, the transcript-rendering path, and the editing auth seam's schedule.

The Go TUI is the existence proof that a thin client composing one renderer with the task API and the chat API can be excellent at all three surfaces. The mobile app is structurally the third instance of that proven composition — 'One Chat Two Surfaces' explicitly anticipated siblings, and the Studio board's own evolution already reached the phone: wave 18's deck replaced kanban with a rail of literal 9:19.5 phone-frame cards, live on main today.

The recommendation, in one paragraph Ship v1 as a Reader-Communicator with teeth: read-only task browsing on the TUI's spine + criteria-first grammar, the full chat floor (send / stream / interrupt / approve-deny with draft continuity), a premium cached paper reader, one search box — plus needs-you push notifications, promoted INTO v1. Three lanes independently converged on the lock-screen approval as THE reason a mobile app should exist; deferring it to v1.5 would ship an app without its killer moment. This is the single deliberate 'new backend' exception, and the server signal to hang it on already exists: the herd layer's Dispatcher-native chat_blocked source and BlockedSweeper (chat charter D57h/D58h). The crown paper must ratify this ruling — it is the largest scope judgment this lane makes.

The three shapes at a glance

DimensionA · Minimal — 'Reader-Communicator'B · Maximal — 'Pocket Studio'C · Sweet Spot — 'Operator's Leash' (v1)
Core ideaThe least app still excellent at reading tasks, chatting, reading papersEverything the platform offers, on a phoneA genuine synthesis: read excellently + act on what needs YOU
Screens~10~30+~14
TasksRead-only: spine list → criteria-first detail; deck-style cardsFull board (deck/gantt/peek), drag claim/close/release, creation with dossierRead-first + needs-you badges; claim/release/close land in v1.5
ChatSessions → transcript; send/stream/interrupt/approve-denyFull ChatLive parity: provider/model/effort/host pickers, bypass arming, fleet rollupMinimal floor + hand-task weld + Doing strip + herd home
PapersCached reader, ~6 block families premium, honest tail degradationReader + block editingReader in v1; prose-only patch-block editing in v2
SearchOne debounced box over tasks+papersFull facets, suggestions, correctionsOne box + fields= projection (~1 KB hits)
PushNoneLock-screen approvals + task alerts + badgesNeeds-you push IN v1 (the deliberate exception)
Token[read, chat]Admin-tier or new seams (editing exceeds every non-admin token today)[read, chat]; +write only at v2
Net-new backendZeroPush channel + per-user editing seam + host managementPush channel only

The staged cut line

StageContainsWhy here and not earlier
v13 tabs + search · full cascade with auto-select + last-location cache · instant cold open from cache (all writes require connectivity) · task read (spine, criteria-first detail) · chat floor (send/stream/interrupt/approve-deny, queued badge, D14 draft continuity) · paper reader · needs-you pushEverything except push is consumption of live endpoints; push is promoted because it is the mobile reason-to-exist
v1.5Task verbs: claim / release / close-with-evidence (the operator's accept button) · needs-you inbox as optional home · session rename/archive · rich question answers (rides the filed /answer route, ct-bl-question-updatedinput)Every task verb drags worker-id identity, epoch-fencing UX and fenced_off/stale_claim error states onto a touch screen — real design work, not real risk
v2Prose-only paper editing (patch-block + per-user :write auth seam) · task creation with dossier · provider/model/effort + execution-host controls · multi-server fast switchEditing is blocked today by the ops route's auth wall (ingest secret OR admin only) — a small, surgical server seam, but a seam nonetheless

The mobile app is not a new product surface. It is the fourth client of machinery that already ships — one renderer, two protocols, and a login flow that already exists.

§

Shape A — the Minimal: 'Reader-Communicator'

The least app that is still excellent. Three tabs and a search box; zero mutations outside chat. Its honest floor is higher than 'read-only' sounds: an agent chat without approve/deny is broken, so the needs-you triple (approval / question / plan — unified server-side, all riding POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/approval with {request_id, decision: allow|deny}) is IN the minimal shape. Task reading ports the TUI grammar that already survived contact with users: one ordered spine (epics → clusters → loose), '+N more' fold rows as tappable affordances, enter-descends/esc-ascends mapped 1:1 to push navigation, criteria-first detail where every section is conditional and color means state only.

#ScreenWhat it showsFeeds from
1Cloud loginRFC-8628 device flow; user_code + verification_uriPOST /v1/auth/device/start → /poll (byte-identical token envelope to normal login)
2Server pickFleet list with health; auto-select if 1; last server cachedCloud GET /v1/barkparks (health_status, last_seen_at; ?scope=all is session-only — a PAT gets 401)
3Scope cascadeWorkspace → project → dataset, each auto-selected when singularGET /api/workspaces, .../projects ('default' first), .../datasets (client pins 'production')
4Tasks tabSpine list: in-flight families first, ready/blocked/open, done ledger lastGET /v1/tasks (stable order — see pagination law), GET /v1/tasks/ready, GET /v1/tasks/prime
5Task detailCriteria-first PortableDoc brief; children; blockers; activityGET /v1/tasks/:id (brief = PortableDoc envelope, TASK-SYSTEM.md:45)
6Chat sessionsSidebar shape; state pills (blocked/working/stalled/idle)GET /v1/chat/sessions (+agent_state per D50h), GET /v1/chat/rollup
7TranscriptBlocks per message; interactive approval/question/plan cards; queued badgeGET /v1/chat/sessions/:id (?since=seq tail refetch), SSE .../events, POST .../messages | interrupt | approval
8Papers tabInstant browse from cached metadata (~1.4 KB/paper)GET /v1/data/query/:dataset/paper?fields=title,description,preview,tags

What the Minimal deliberately does NOT have No task verbs, no task creation, no paper editing, no notifications, no host/provider controls, no multi-server switching, no media browsing. Deliberate absences are the shape's identity: every one of them is reachable by a deep link into Studio (the TUI already ships o → Studio task URL as an SSH-friendly escape hatch; the app inherits the same move).

Shape B — the Maximal: 'Pocket Studio'

Everything the platform offers. The task tab becomes the full board — deck of phone-frame cards (already designed and live at /admin/projects, board_live.ex wave 18), gantt expand (wave 21), peek family-tree inspector (waves 13-15), drag restage through the same fenced claim/close/release primitives agents use (restage_plan/4, board.ex:645-662). Chat reaches full ChatLive parity: ~40 handle_events including provider/model/effort pickers, execution-target and registered-host selection, bypass arming ceremony, fleet rollup herd view, slash commands, context ring. Papers gain block editing. Plus media, multi-server fast-switch, and lock-screen push approvals.

The maximal case, argued honestly For: Studio LiveView already proves every interaction server-side — a maximal client is transcription, not invention; the ChatLive render-vocab census gives a complete parts list. Against, and decisive for this lane: three of its pillars are NOT 'just a client'. (1) Native push has zero existing machinery — grep across api/lib and cloud/lib finds no APNs/FCM; the filed scc-w13-notify-channels task is Web Push + webhook only. (2) Paper block editing exceeds EVERY non-admin token today: all three ops routes sit behind RequireIngestToken (shared ingest secret OR admin api_token — require_ingest_token.ex has no write/chat path). (3) Nine ChatLive surfaces are LiveView-only and never reach any client today (MCP entity chips, thinking pulse, compaction notice, context ring, slash menu, provider/host pickers, bypass ceremony, Doing strip, session chrome) — each must be reproduced, proxied, or scoped out. The Maximal is a fine v3 horizon, not a v1.

Shape C — the Sweet Spot: 'Operator's Leash'

A genuine synthesis, not a midpoint: the Minimal's reading excellence plus the one thing a phone is FOR — being reachable when your agents need you. Three welds define it. Weld 1, chat⇄tasks: Studio already prototyped the hand-task picker (Tasks.ready limit 8, chat_live.ex:544) and the Doing strip above the composer (:281-282, :555) — the app ports both, making 'hand this ready task to the running session' a first-class phone gesture. Weld 2, universal search: FTS already spans tasks + papers with facets and a fields= projection at ~1 KB per hit. Weld 3, needs-you push: one notification channel keyed on the pending-ask rows the BlockedSweeper already watches (D58h keys on ask rows, never agent_state), deep-linking straight into the transcript's approval card. The herd home (blocked > stalled > working > idle, deterministic sort, 150s stall badge — herd.go:245-287) is the natural launch screen for an operator with more than one session.

The open home-surface question — three equal tabs vs a cross-surface needs-you inbox (approvals + blocked tasks + lease-expired in one feed) vs chat-as-home — is left deliberately open. No existing surface has designed a cross-surface inbox, so it has no prior art to port; the safe v1 answer is three tabs with a needs-you badge count, letting the inbox graduate to home in v1.5 if usage proves it.

§

What we learned — findings, surprises, corrected premises

Fourteen storm probes fed this lane. The central discovery held: the three surfaces are one rendering problem plus two protocols. But several of this lane's founding beliefs were corrected by evidence, and the corrections change the product brief:

Premise going inVerdictEvidence
'18 block families lack reader CSS' — mobile reader must fear the tailSTALE — already fixed on origin/mainPR #5651 (bbf110e19) styled all 18 families, mobile-390 verified; PR #5656 added a compose-time coverage gate; the 'gap' was a stale local checkout
The app token should be [read, write, chat]WRONG — [read, chat] sufficesAll /v1/tasks* routes take ANY valid token (tasks.ex:432-461, bare RequireToken); reads need 'read'; chat needs workspace-bound 'chat'; write is only for /v1/data/mutate
'Zero push machinery exists'Half right — refinedNative APNs/FCM: truly zero (grep-proven). But a Notifier seam exists: scc-w13-notify-channels (open, 0/4 criteria) plans Web Push + webhook channels — a seam to extend, not a void
The pull events feed makes task sync trivialTRUE for deltas — but the LIST is a trapGET /v1/tasks default order is desc(updated_at): offset paging skips/duplicates whenever any row is touched mid-walk; no cursor exists on list/ready; the TUI pulls limit=1000 and confesses truncation (fetch.go:38-41)
Chat approval can carry rich answersNO — allow/deny onlyD22 forbids caller-supplied updatedInput; rich AskUserQuestion answers are a FILED, unbuilt /answer route (ct-bl-question-updatedinput, open, 0/3)
Login/token exchange needs designNO — reuse, don't inventbp-login-ux charter ships an RFC-8628 device flow + fleet auto-pick (n==1 fast path, decision 19) already merged for the CLI wizard; mobile is its fourth consumer
Paper editing is a renderer problemNO — it is an AUTH problemThe editing machinery exists (pd-everything-editable, 19 children, graded A-); the wall is RequireIngestToken (ingest secret OR admin only). The cheap seam: Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — a surgical plug change
Search can power typeaheadNO — debounce and cacheLive-measured 249-594 ms server-side per query (~457 ms via CLI); the ≤40 ms goal was never reached and its next lever sits in 'considering'; fields= projection is real (25x) but is NOT a declared CLI flag — raw HTTP callers get it

Findings that make the app cheaper than it looks

  • One renderer covers everything that matters: @barkpark/react dispatches 66 block types (CI-pinned), including all 6 chat blocks; the only missing types are the 15-item schema/field family (field-*, arrayOf, composite, codelist, localizedText, embed) — structured-data blocks, not prose or chat. Chat has zero renderer-parity risk on any shell choice.
  • The interaction grammar transfers wholesale: spine ordering, fold rows, criteria-first conditional detail, color-as-state-only, the deck's 9:19.5 phone cards, the double-press close guard, the 8s interrupt wedge, the 150s herd stall badge — all shipped, all numbered decisions with file anchors.
  • The pull keyset events feed (GET /v1/tasks/events?since → {events, cursor, has_more}) is background-kill-safe — cache the cursor, replay on foreground — strictly better for phones than SSE, which iOS suspends. The platform accidentally built the ideal mobile sync primitive.
  • Cross-device draft continuity already exists: D14 PATCHes draft/mode/model/effort on leave and re-GETs on resume — a draft typed on the phone resumes in the desktop TUI with no new server work.
  • Paper payload economics are settled: 1.4 KB metadata / 34 KB blocks / 137 KB full (median, measured live) — prefetch dozens of papers for offline browse, fetch blocks on open.
  • Reader excellence is cheap: 5 block types cover 92% of all authored block instances; nail ~6 families beautifully, degrade the tail honestly (all 18 formerly-unstyled families now have CSS on main).

Findings that constrain the design

  • Tenancy depth differs per tab — the wish's 5-level cascade lands at a DIFFERENT level per surface: chat is workspace-scoped (RequireChatAccess), tasks are flat host-root (any token), papers/data are dataset-scoped. The app's scope object must carry all levels; each tab consumes the level it needs. One cascade UI, three effective scopes — a crown-level fact, not a bug.
  • Media in a WebView: paper image src values are bare unsigned /media/files/<path> strings; serving is public by DEFAULT visibility but token/private assets silently 403 (a WebView <img> cannot attach Bearer headers, and nothing pre-signs at render time). Honest v1 promise: excellent reading for public-visibility media; scoped/private needs a signed-src or fetch-to-blob shim later. studio_chat.ex:2441 already flags this exact leak class.
  • Chat requires a live managed runtime or enrolled chat host — a phone cannot run the CLI. Live probe: all 37 guerrilla sessions are provider=claude, execution_target=managed; on a vanilla self-hosted box the chat tab may be dead-on-arrival and needs the empty-state/onboarding screen no sibling surface has designed (lane-3 territory; the brief cannot dodge it).
  • The chat-transcript rendering fork is real and couples to the shell bet: this lane's evidence favors persisted blocks through the shared renderer (D8 ships blocks server-side; 6/6 JS parity); the shell lane argues native rendering from source_markdown. One ruling, in the crown, after the shell verdict.
  • iOS reality checks (if the shell is a PWA): installed PWAs get NO storage-eviction exemption (heuristic safety via persist() + regular opens), Web Push is install-only, SSE never survives backgrounding — reconnect-on-foreground is law regardless of shell. The 'instant open + remember where I was' promise is only CONDITIONALLY honorable as a PWA; native/Expo carries none of these caveats (expo/fetch streams since SDK 52; App Store risk is low — guideline 4.8 explicitly exempts first-party-account apps; keep all billing web-side).
§

How the system works today — anchors a builder can jump to

The chat wire contract (the app's most intricate dependency)

POST /v1/chat/sessions                {mode?,model?,effort?} -> 201 session (id = CLI --resume key)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions?archived=      -> {sessions:[...]} sidebar shape (+agent_state, D50h)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions/:id[?since=n]  -> full session + messages seq-asc; assistant rows carry
                                         blocks (server FromMarkdown, D8) AND source_markdown
PATCH /v1/chat/sessions/:id           {draft|mode|model_choice|effort_choice|title} strict allowlist
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/messages   {content} -> 202 {accepted:true}   (queued badge = client-only, D12)
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/interrupt  -> 202 {request_id} (ack is semantically EMPTY; truth = result frame)
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/approval   {request_id, decision:allow|deny} -> 204  (D22: nothing richer)
GET  /v1/chat/sessions/:id/events     SSE: replay (id:<seq> event:message) then live (event:chat,
                                         verbatim provider frames, no id); event:permission; event:exit;
                                         keepalive 30s. Turn settles ONLY at the terminal result frame (D8).
GET  /v1/chat/events                  fleet stream: snapshot(50-cap)/state/heartbeat frames,
                                         Last-Event-ID = opaque epoch:seq (D45h)
Auth: [:api, :require_chat_access] — global admin OR workspace-bound 'chat' token (Connectors D18).
Bounds: title/request_id <=256B; content/draft <=64KiB. Transcript window: 500 rows.
Sessions spawn lazily on first send, never on mount; reopen replays history instantly.

The client discipline is fully codified in the chat TUI's numbered decisions — the mobile parity checklist is: D5 (caller owns the SSE cursor, seeded from max persisted seq), D8 (settle at result frame; then ONE tail refetch with ?since), D9 (live deltas are truth until settle, then discarded), D11 (interrupt mid-turn; 8s client wedge timer force-degrades), D12 (queued badge is pure client state), D14 (PATCH continuity set on leave, re-GET on resume), D51h (idle back-gesture detaches, never interrupts), D53h (stall computed fresh at render, never stored). Reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary replaces any assumption of a durable stream.

The permission matrix (smallest-token proof)

Route familyPipelineRequired permissionAnchor
/v1/tasks* (all 16) + /v1/fleet/*[:api, :require_token]ANY valid token — claim/close are workflow ops, not doc mutationstasks.ex:432-461; router.ex:461-463

Task reading, sync, and the pagination law

  • GET /v1/tasks: limit clamped [1,1000], offset [0,100000]; default order desc(updated_at), desc(id) — UNSTABLE for paging a live ledger (3400+ tasks under constant multi-agent mutation). Stable orders already exist: parent= filtered views use asc(inserted_at), asc(id); /v1/tasks/ready uses priority asc, inserted_at asc, id asc. Mobile law: never bulk-sync the default order; page a stable order, or prime + events.
  • GET /v1/tasks/events?since=<id> → {ok, events, cursor, has_more}, monotonic cursor, ≤500/page — the mobile sync spine: persist the cursor, replay on foreground.
  • Task brief is a presentation-grade PortableDoc envelope; detail rendering = the same problem as papers (one renderer). Criteria-first reader order is shipped TUI law (detail_render.go D15) even though its doc codification is still an uncommitted local edit.
  • The board's deck (default view, wave 18) proves the phone card: 9:19.5 phone-frame cards, click expands to family gantt (wave 21); the kanban drag surface does NOT transfer to portrait — the spine/deck/peek lineage does. BoardLive has exactly 9 handle_events; restage fans into claim/close/release/refuse via pure restage_plan/4.

The login cascade, level by level

LevelEndpointRow shapeAuto-select signal
IdentityCloud GET /v1/meuser + teams[]—
ServerCloud GET /v1/barkparks (?scope=all is session-only; a PAT gets 401)rich: health_status, agent_status, last_seen_at, mode, url …health hints yes; no per-user 'last visited' — client caches it
WorkspaceGET /api/workspacesbare {id, slug, name}, alphabeticalnone — client counts and remembers
ProjectGET /api/workspaces/:ws/projectsbare {id, slug, name}'default' slug sorts FIRST (tenancy.ex:858-869) — the one real server hint
DatasetGET .../projects/:proj/datasetsbare {id, slug, name}, alphabeticalnone — no 'production'-first despite it being the bootstrapped default; client pins it (or add the ordering hint server-side, a 2-line change)
§

Files likely to change

The dominant fact: v1 is overwhelmingly a NEW client plus a handful of small, named server seams. Nothing in the existing surfaces needs restructuring for the Sweet Spot's v1.

PathWhy it changesBlast radius
mobile/** (new tree; final name per shell lane)The entire app: cascade, three tabs, search, cache, push registrationNone — greenfield; CI needs a new gate lane

api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/require_ingest_token.ex (or a sibling plug)v2 editing seam: per-user :write branch via the existing Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3Medium — auth-boundary change; needs cross-tenant negative tests (D19a pattern)

§

Risks and unknowns

Held risks (accepted into the recommendation) (1) Push in v1 makes the first release depend on the one genuinely new backend build — if it slips, v1 ships as the Minimal and push becomes v1.1; that graceful degradation is exactly why the shapes are staged. (2) Chat-tab dead-on-arrival on servers without a managed runtime — needs the onboarding empty state; severity depends on lane 3's runtime findings. (3) The eventual-editing ambition contradicts the v1 token design ([read,chat] cannot edit papers); resolved only by scheduling the auth seam in v2, and the crown must carry that dependency visibly. (4) Offset paging on the live ledger will corrupt task lists if a builder ignores the stable-order rule — the epic brief must state it as law. (5) If the shell is a PWA, the cache promise is conditional on iOS heuristics and Web Push is install-only; the shell lane's verdict may force native for push alone.
Judgment calls left explicitly to the user / epic strategist (1) RATIFY push-in-v1 (this lane recommends yes; it breaks 'new client only' purity). (2) The v1 task-verb line: pure read (recommended) vs shipping claim/close in v1. (3) Home surface: three tabs with badges (recommended for v1) vs needs-you inbox as home vs chat-as-home. (4) Whether the dataset level appears as a real cascade screen or lives only inside a scope switcher (auto-select hides it 99% of the time either way). (5) The chat-transcript rendering fork — persisted blocks through the shared renderer vs native from source_markdown — rule it once, in the crown, after the shell verdict. (6) Paper-editing staging: prose-only v2 (recommended) vs 'continue in Studio' handoff forever.
§

Coverage appendix — what was checked, found, and NOT found

Absences are decisions-in-waiting. Everything below was verified against origin/main (the local checkout is dirty and provably stale in places) or measured live on guerrilla during the storm.

CheckedResultNote

TUI task + chat grammars (keys → endpoints)FOUNDprogram.go, actions.go, keys.go from origin/main (local internal/chat is 2 PRs stale)
Renderer matrix across Elixir/JS/GoFOUND75-81 / 66 / 82 types; the JS gap = exactly the 15 field-family types; chat 6/6 everywhere
Login cascade endpoints, all 5 levelsFOUNDNo level lacks a list endpoint; below Cloud all rows are bare {id,slug,name}
Live guerrilla proof (chat, search, paper payloads)FOUND/v1/chat/rollup 200; 37 claude/managed sessions; search 249-594 ms; payload table measured
Native push (APNs/FCM) anywhere in api/ or cloud/NOT FOUNDZero hits — v1's one new backend build; scc-w13 (Web Push) is filed but open and browser-only
Mobile shell prior art (PWA/React Native/Expo) in repo or corpusNOT FOUNDGreenfield; only a false-positive transitive dep name in pnpm-lock
Per-user path onto the paper block-ops routeNOT FOUNDRequireIngestToken has exactly two doors: ingest secret, admin token; the :write seam is designed but unbuilt

This paper is the product-shapes lane of the Barkpark Tasks mobile preparation stack. The crown paper — barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone — combines it with the identity-cascade, chat-third-client, tasks-papers-reading, and shell-and-cache lanes, and must rule on the four forks this lane leaves open: push-in-v1, the v1 mutation line, the transcript-rendering path, and the editing auth seam's schedule.

The task surface ports the TUI spine + criteria-first grammar and the board deck's phone-frame card language.

title: Barkpark Tasks: Three Rival Shapes — the Minimal, the Maximal, and the Sweet Spot
